title: rule-set.v1
description: A versioned, immutable set of declarative rules evaluated against a `context-document.v1.json` (A§55, plan §7 DEC-1/DEC-4). Two kinds share this shape: `RULES` sets carry business decision logic (which treatment), `POLICY` sets carry global constraints that outrank everything else (A§54) — policy sets are global and are never pinned per strategy, so a strategy document references a rule set but never a policy set. The DSL is deliberately not Turing-complete: no loops, no arithmetic, no user functions, no quantifiers over arrays. That is what makes a decision deterministic, replayable from its input snapshot, explainable in reason codes, and parity-testable against the legacy engine (A§88). Evaluation is first-match-wins ordered by (`priority` DESC, `ruleId` ASC) — a total order, so two engines cannot disagree; a leaf whose `field` is missing from the context evaluates to false and records `FIELD_MISSING` in the trace rather than raising (LIB-9 `ruledsl`). Published sets are immutable: DEC-4 rejects a mutation of a PUBLISHED version with 409, and a change ships as a new `version`.

ruleSetId.description: Stable identifier of the rule set family, e.g. `EARLY_COLLECTION_RULES` or `GLOBAL_CONTACT_POLICY`. Together with `version` it is the primary key; a strategy's `ruleSetRef` names both.

kind.description: `RULES` = business decision logic; outcomes may SELECT_TREATMENT or SUPPRESS. `POLICY` = global policy constraints; outcomes may only narrow (SUPPRESS, FORBID_CHANNEL) and never select a treatment, which is CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 and A§54 expressed in the schema rather than in prose. Both directions are enforced below by `if/then`, so a policy set that tries to pick a treatment — the classic way an "optimization override" sneaks in — fails validation at publish time.

version.description: Major version of this rule set, starting at 1 and incremented on every publish. The meaning of a published (`ruleSetId`, `version`) pair never changes; decisions record the exact pair they used so an audit can replay them.

effectiveFrom.description: First business date (UTC calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`) on which this version may be used.

effectiveTo.description: Last business date on which this version may be used, inclusive, or NULL for open-ended. Required and nullable rather than optional: "no end date" is a decision someone made, and an audit must see it stated.

rules.description: The rules, in authoring order. Authoring order carries no meaning — evaluation order is (`priority` DESC, `ruleId` ASC). `ruleId` is unique within the set and Σ of matching rules is irrelevant: exactly one rule matches (the first in that order) and it alone supplies the outcome and reason code. DEC-4 validates uniqueness and that every `field` exists in the context field catalogue and every `reasonCode` in registries/reason-codes.v1.json.

allOf.title: RULES sets may not forbid a channel
allOf.description: FORBID_CHANNEL is a policy narrowing and exists only in a POLICY set. A business rule set that forbids a channel would put a constraint outside the policy precedence chain, where the post-selection guard cannot re-validate it.

allOf.title: POLICY sets narrow only, never select
allOf.description: CLAUDE.md hard rule 2 / A§54: constraints expose narrowing only. A POLICY set that could SELECT_TREATMENT would let policy pick outcomes and, worse, let a treatment choice claim policy precedence.

code.title: Code
code.description: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE identifier: starts with a letter, 3–64 characters. The platform's vocabulary shape for ids, reason codes, treatment codes and segment names — stable, greppable, safe in a URL and in a log line.

fieldPath.title: FieldPath
fieldPath.description: Dot path into the context document, e.g. `delinquency.dpd`. Must exist in `context-field-catalogue.v1.json`: DEC-4 rejects an unknown path with a 400 naming the field, so a renamed context field cannot silently turn a condition permanently false. The catalogue also supplies the comparison type and unit.

scalar.title: ComparisonValue
scalar.description: A single comparison value: string, number or boolean. NEVER null — absence is tested with IS_NULL / NOT_NULL, so a null here would be a second, ambiguous way to ask the same question. A catalogue `number` field may be compared against a JSON number (`35`) or a decimal string (`"500.00"`); both are parsed as exact decimals, which is what lets major-unit money strings be compared without a float. A `date` field compares against `YYYY-MM-DD` or an RFC3339 UTC timestamp. `boolean` fields compare only against `true`/`false`, `string` fields only against strings (exact equality; no substring, no regex, no case folding).

condition.title: Condition
condition.description: A leaf comparison. The permitted shape of `value` follows from `op`, modelled as a `oneOf` over four op families so that an impossible combination is rejected by the schema rather than by a runtime surprise: presence ops carry NO `value` at all, scalar comparisons carry exactly one, BETWEEN carries an inclusive two-element `[low, high]`, and IN / NOT_IN carry a non-empty set. The four branches are mutually exclusive on `op`, so exactly one always matches and the validator's error names the family that failed.

oneOf.title: presence ops (IS_NULL, NOT_NULL)
oneOf.description: No `value` is permitted: `additionalProperties: false` with `value` undeclared is what rejects `{op: IS_NULL, value: null}`.

op.description: IS_NULL matches when the field is JSON null or absent from the context; NOT_NULL is its exact complement.

oneOf.title: scalar comparison ops (EQ, NE, GT, GTE, LT, LTE)

op.description: Ordering ops (GT, GTE, LT, LTE) are valid only for catalogue types `number` and `date`; EQ/NE apply to every type. The type check is the catalogue's job at publish time (DEC-4), not this schema's — the schema cannot know which type `field` names.

value.description: Exactly `[low, high]`, INCLUSIVE at both ends (`dpd BETWEEN [31, 60]` matches 31 and 60) — the convention business users assume when they write "31 to 60 days", and the one LIB-9 implements. `minItems`/`maxItems` are both 2, so a three-element range or a bare scalar is a validation error rather than a rule that silently ignores a bound. `low <= high` is checked at publish time (the schema cannot compare siblings).

Non-empty set of comparison values. `uniqueItems` because a repeated member is always an authoring mistake, and an empty set is rejected because `IN []` (never true) and `NOT_IN []` (always true) are both traps a reviewer will read as the opposite.

conditionGroup.title: ConditionGroup
conditionGroup.description: PUBLIC ENTRY POINT for a boolean condition tree — the shape `strategy-document.v1.json` references for `eligibility` and segment `when` clauses, and the shape of a rule's `when`. A group is `{"all": [...]}` (conjunction) XOR `{"any": [...]}` (disjunction), never both: the two branches are a `oneOf` and each forbids the other's key, so `{"all": [...], "any": [...]}` — whose meaning nobody can guess — fails validation. Members are either leaf conditions or nested groups. NESTING IS CAPPED AT 5 LEVELS, and the cap is mechanical, not advisory: `conditionGroupLevel1`…`conditionGroupLevel5` form a finite chain and a level-5 group accepts leaf conditions only, so a 6-level tree cannot be expressed at all. The cap exists because a condition tree deeper than five levels is unreviewable by the business owner who has to sign it off, and because a bounded grammar keeps the evaluator's cost predictable. An empty `all` is vacuously TRUE and is the documented DEFAULT segment / unconditional-eligibility idiom; an empty `any` is rejected, since a group that can never match is always an authoring error.

conditionGroupLevel1.title: ConditionGroup (nesting level 1 of 5)
conditionGroupLevel1.description: Outermost group. Members may be leaf conditions or level-2 groups.

all.description: Conjunction. Empty = vacuously true (the DEFAULT segment idiom).

any.description: Disjunction. Must be non-empty: an empty `any` never matches.

conditionGroupLevel5.title: ConditionGroup (nesting level 5 of 5 — leaves only)
conditionGroupLevel5.description: The deepest permitted group: its members are leaf conditions only. This is where the depth cap bites — there is no `nodeLevel6`, so a sixth level of nesting has no schema to validate against and the document is rejected.

ruleId.description: Identifier of the rule, unique within the set and stable across versions where the rule's intent is unchanged — it is recorded in the decision trace as `matchedRuleId`, and it is the tie-break (ASC) when two rules share a priority, which is what makes evaluation a total order.

priority.description: Evaluation priority; HIGHER wins. Rules are ordered (`priority` DESC, `ruleId` ASC) and the first whose `when` matches supplies the outcome — later rules are not evaluated. Leave gaps (100, 200, 300) so a rule can be inserted between two others without renumbering a published set.

when.description: Condition tree that must be true for this rule to match. `{"all": []}` is an unconditional rule — the catch-all at the lowest priority.

action.title: Action
action.description: The outcome of a matched rule, modelled as a `oneOf` per outcome so that the fields which are meaningful for that outcome are required and the ones that are not are forbidden — a SUPPRESS carrying a `treatmentCode` is dead configuration that a reader would take for a selection.

oneOf.title: SELECT_TREATMENT
oneOf.description: Choose a treatment by code (RULES sets only). The channel comes from the strategy's `treatments[]` entry for that code, so it is not repeated here and cannot contradict it.

treatmentCode.description: Must be one of the `treatments[].treatmentCode` values of every strategy that references this rule set — validated when the strategy transitions to TEST (DEC-3), because a rule pointing at a treatment the strategy does not offer would decide nothing at runtime.

reasonCode.description: Registry reason code explaining the match, e.g. `DPD_31_60`. REQUIRED on every outcome: an unexplainable decision is not shippable (A§58), and the registry is closed, so DEC-4 rejects an unknown code.

oneOf.title: SUPPRESS
oneOf.description: Take no action on this subject. Valid in both kinds: a business rule suppresses (e.g. an arrangement is being honoured), and a policy rule suppresses as a narrowing constraint.

oneOf.title: FORBID_CHANNEL
oneOf.description: Remove one channel from consideration — POLICY sets only (enforced by the `kind` guard above). This is the only channel-level narrowing on the platform: it cannot select, cannot re-permit, and the post-selection guard re-applies it to the chosen treatment, so an optimizer that prefers the forbidden channel still cannot dispatch on it (A§54, CLAUDE.md hard rule 2).

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: Delivery channel of a treatment. `CALL` is a collector call task rather than an automated send, which is why it is a channel here and `CALL_TASK` is the treatment type in strategy documents.
